newsitem.title: UK: BA says more flights operate despite strike.
newsitem.headline: BA says more flights operate despite strike.

text.p: British Airways Plc, mired in a damaging dispute with cabin crew over pay and cost cutting, said even more of its flights were getting away on Friday as more staff turned up to work.
Thousands of passengers have been stranded by the cabin crew strike, which started on Wednesday and is expected to end early on Saturday.

BA now faces a fresh strike by catering staff, which rejected the plan to sell its catering division by a vote of 551-178. The catering union will meet on Monday to decide whether to call its own 24-hour strike which could suck in check-in staff and baggage handlers.
In the current conflict, BA claimed it was persuading cabin crew to return to work: "Far more members of (cabin crew) staff than expected have been coming in," a BA spokesman said.
"We expect to have about 80 percent of all our normal network services including franchises operating today."
But the main union representing the cabin crew denied BA's claims that the strike was crumbling.
